review_evidence: A keyword grep (theorem|lemma|def|structure|class|instance|inductive|abbrev|example|axiom|opaque|macro|syntax|elab|notation) over all 893 files found 4 files with no match. I read all 4 completely.

HexGraphIso/Sparse/Tactic.lean (3239 B) and HexGraphIso/Sparse/TacticSupport.lean (8697 B) hold `meta def` declarations (proveColored, proveBare, the @[graph_iso_extension] extension, findWitness, findCandidates, proveIsIso, proveKey, proveDifferent) and a `meta opaque evalNat`. The initial grep missed the `meta` modifier. These declarations are the graph_iso tactic interface, so both files stay.

HexGraphIso/Nauty/Search/VSet.lean (684 B) has only `module`, three `public import`s (VSet.Basic, VSet.Card, VSet.Nat) and a module docstring about packed vertex sets. HexGraphIso/Sparse.lean (982 B) has only `module`, nine `public import`s and a module docstring. Both are import aggregators. FILTER-007 keeps them primary-eligible and ranks them as navigation-import-only, so both stay.

The largest file, HexGraphIso/Kernel/CheckKey.lean (129425 B), is hand-written source with a long design docstring and 252 theorem/lemma/def lines (for example Kernel.checkKey_eq and Kernel.not_isomorphic_of_checkKeys). It is not generated data.

The other large files (Nauty/Search/Refine.lean 91373 B, Nauty/Spec/CanonSpec.lean 82136 B, Nauty/SmallCell/Shapes.lean 80285 B, HexPolySmith/Correctness/Invariant.lean 75771 B) are in the declaration-bearing set.
The smallest files (Nauty/Spec/Traced.lean 575 B, Nauty/Policy/KeyComplete.lean 616 B) each contain a declaration.

A grep for auto-generated|do not edit|generated by matched 10 files. In each match I checked, the phrase is mathematical ("the subgroup generated by a list of permutations" in HexGraphIso/Generated.lean, "the ideal generated by the k x k minors" in HexPolySmith/Divisor.lean) and is not a code-generation marker.
summary: Surveyed all 893 listed files (6,549,005 bytes, all .lean, all present in reservoir-sources/kim-em__hex-dev): 861 under HexGraphIso (529 in HexGraphIso/Nauty/Sparse), 11 HexDeterminantalIdealMathlib, 11 HexPolyMathlib, 10 HexPolySmith. Grepped every file for declaration keywords, ranked by size, and grepped for generated-file markers. The files are original Lean 4 source for a verified nauty-style graph isomorphism/canonical labelling library, Smith normal form over polynomials, and determinantal ideals, with about 5,600 theorem/lemma lines in total. Two files are import-only modules with module docstrings; under FILTER-007 they stay primary-eligible and are handled by ranking, not exclusion. No file meets the FILTER-002/FILTER-004 bar, so every file is retained.

Step.lean:30-362 defines PairStep structure, pairStep constructor, and proves pairStep_pivot_shape, pairStep_pivot_size_lt_left, pairStep_apply, pairStep_forward_inverse, pairStep_inverse_forward with detailed algebraic reasoning over DensePoly F; includes #guard executable checks on 14 polynomial pairs
summary: Inspected both changed files. HexPolyMathlib/Interpret.lean defines an interpretation function from executable dense polynomials to Mathlib polynomials with 20+ theorems about its algebraic properties (coeff, zero, degree, add, mul, derivative, eval, divMod, gcd, bezout). HexPolySmith/Step.lean defines the monic-normalizing two-row Bezout step for polynomial Smith reduction with 8 main theorems (pivot shape, size decrease, forward/inverse matrix correctness) plus executable regression checks. Both files contain substantial original formal mathematical declarations and proofs — no pure import modules, no generated code, no duplicates.
